source.snippet: Add a thumbnail track to the CMAF output — sprite sheets plus a WebVTT index, PUT to the same ingest as the media segments — so a browser player can show a scrub preview across a long DVR window... Coarse scrubbing across a 60-minute window cannot decode arbitrary positions in real time. Without a preview, dragging the scrub bar is blind: the operator sees nothing until they release and the player seeks. [Issue #123]: Add a configurable DVR window to the CMAF output so browser clients can seek back over a long history — including to points before the client joined the stream.

problem_statement: Browser-based live video players using CMAF/HLS lack built-in support for long DVR windows with scrub preview (sprite sheet thumbnails + WebVTT), forcing engineering teams to build custom solutions from scratch for every streaming product.
target_segment: Streaming infrastructure engineers and media tech companies building browser-based DVR or live replay players on top of CMAF/HLS pipelines
notes: Two related GitHub issues on the same project (bilbycast-edge) both filed the same day, indicating active engineering investment in browser DVR. The pain — blind scrubbing and capped DVR history — is well-known in streaming infrastructure. A hosted CMAF thumbnail/DVR window generation service or open-source library with commercial support could serve media tech teams. Buyer evidence is implicit (engineering time cost, existing paid streaming infra). Signal strength kept at 2 as this is a single project's internal tracker.
